chiefComplaint: A dark raised spot has changed shape and bled once.

historyAnswers.Onset and duration: The change began gradually over several weeks.
historyAnswers.Itch versus pain: No pain today; one episode of bleeding after friction.
historyAnswers.New medications: No new medication in the past two months.
historyAnswers.Sun exposure and tanning: Outdoor exposure is intermittent; no tanning bed use.
historyAnswers.Personal and family skin cancer history: The spot is new and evolving; review personal/family skin cancer history and UV exposure.
historyAnswers.Pregnancy and contraception status: Pregnancy possibility and goals should be reviewed before teratogenic therapies.
historyAnswers.Systemic symptoms: No constitutional symptoms or palpable regional nodes on focused exam.
historyAnswers.Focused clue: The lesion has enlarged and changed color over several months; ask about prior melanoma, atypical nevi, and ultraviolet exposure.

examFindings.General appearance: Fictional teaching patient; assess vital signs and overall appearance in real practice.
examFindings.Focused lesion exam: An asymmetric, irregularly contoured dark brown-to-black lobulated plaque/nodule with focal erythema.
examFindings.Full skin exam: Assess distribution and extent beyond the pictured site; no constitutional symptoms or palpable regional nodes on focused exam.
examFindings.Mucosal exam: No additional abnormality found on this maneuver.
examFindings.Nails and hair: No additional abnormality found on this maneuver.
examFindings.Lymph nodes: No palpable regional lymphadenopathy; assess by site and risk.
examFindings.Nikolsky sign: No additional abnormality found on this maneuver.
examFindings.Wood lamp: No additional abnormality found on this maneuver.
examFindings.Dermoscopy: Asymmetric network and irregular dots/globules; concerning evolution.

acceptableTreatments.name: urgent biopsy and expedited specialist pathway
acceptableTreatments.reason: urgent complete diagnostic biopsy with appropriate margins; stage after pathology

unacceptableTreatments.name: High-potency topical corticosteroid on face or folds
unacceptableTreatments.reason: Site-related atrophy risk; choose site-appropriate treatment.

unacceptableTreatments.name: Systemic corticosteroid for an undifferentiated rash
unacceptableTreatments.reason: May obscure diagnosis and worsen some infections.

unacceptableTreatments.name: Methotrexate without baseline assessment
unacceptableTreatments.reason: Requires screening, labs, pregnancy precautions, and specialist oversight.

unacceptableTreatments.name: Biologic therapy without infection screening
unacceptableTreatments.reason: Requires appropriate screening and specialist plan.

unacceptableTreatments.name: Spironolactone without pregnancy and contraindication review
unacceptableTreatments.reason: Review pregnancy goals, relevant contraindications, and monitoring before use.

unacceptableTreatments.name: Isotretinoin without pregnancy prevention steps when applicable
unacceptableTreatments.reason: Major teratogenic risk; follow current prescribing safeguards.

teachingPearl: An evolving, asymmetric, variegated pigmented lesion requires prompt biopsy with appropriate technique and staging follow-up.
traps: Anchoring on morphology without asking about timing
Using a potent topical steroid on thin or intertriginous skin
Missing medication timing or mucosal symptoms
Ordering biopsy without a decision-changing question
